title: Acute infectious diarrhoea and dysentery (adult)
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Rehydrate first (ORS, or Ringer lactate for severe dehydration). Most watery diarrhoea needs no stool test or antibiotic; treat cholera with dehydration, dysentery, severe travellers' diarrhoea and sepsis, preferring azithromycin where fluoroquinolone resistance is common.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Acute diarrhoea: 3 or more loose stools in 24 hours for less than 14 days. Separate watery diarrhoea from dysentery (visible blood or mucus, fever, tenesmus).
Grade dehydration: some (thirst, dry mouth, sunken eyes, tachycardia, reduced urine) or severe (lethargy, hypotension, weak pulse, poor skin turgor, oliguria).
Suspect cholera with profuse painless rice-water stools and rapid severe dehydration, especially in outbreaks or the monsoon.

Red flags: temperature 38.5°C or more, bloody stools, severe abdominal pain or tenderness, sepsis, older age, pregnancy, immunocompromise, recent antibiotics or hospital stay (C. difficile), symptoms beyond 7 days.
Exclude mimics: appendicitis, obstruction, DKA, sepsis from another source, malaria, and drug causes.

sections.title: Rehydration
items: Some dehydration: reduced osmolarity ORS (sodium 75 mEq/L, glucose 75 mmol/L), about 75 mL/kg over 4 hours, then replace ongoing losses.

Severe dehydration or shock: IV Ringer lactate (0.9% saline if unavailable) 100 mL/kg: 30 mL/kg in 30 minutes, then 70 mL/kg over 2.5 hours, reassessing frequently. Go slower in the elderly and in heart or kidney failure.
Start ORS as soon as the patient can drink, and continue a normal diet.
Check and correct potassium and bicarbonate in moderate to severe cases; hypokalaemia is common in cholera.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Most acute watery diarrhoea needs no stool test.

Stool culture or multiplex PCR (plus C. difficile testing if recent antibiotics) for fever, bloody or mucoid stools, severe cramps or tenderness, sepsis, immunocompromise, outbreaks, or persistent symptoms (IDSA 2017).
Electrolytes, urea, creatinine and CBC in moderate or severe illness; blood cultures if febrile or septic.
Stool microscopy for Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites or Giardia when suggested by the history.

sections.title: Antibiotics: when and which
items: No antibiotic for acute watery diarrhoea in adults, except cholera with dehydration and moderate to severe travellers' diarrhoea.
Cholera: doxycycline 300 mg orally single dose, or azithromycin 1 g orally single dose (use azithromycin in pregnancy) (ICMR 2022).
Dysentery (bloody diarrhoea): treat for Shigella promptly (ICMR 2022) with ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 3 days, or ceftriaxone 2 g IV if oral therapy is not possible.

Where Shigella fluoroquinolone resistance is common, azithromycin 500 mg daily for 3 days is widely used instead. Send stool culture: ICMR notes Shigella resistance to azithromycin and cefixime is approaching 20%.
Campylobacter: azithromycin 500 mg orally once daily for 3 days (fluoroquinolone resistance is high in South Asia).
Travellers' diarrhoea, moderate or severe: azithromycin 1 g single dose or 500 mg daily for 3 days (CDC Yellow Book).

Amoebic dysentery: metronidazole 500 mg three times daily (ICMR 5 days; many references use 7 to 10 days), then a luminal agent such as diloxanide furoate 500 mg three times daily for 10 days. Giardiasis: metronidazole 250 mg three times daily for 5 days.
Avoid antibiotics in suspected Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (bloody diarrhoea with little or no fever): they raise the risk of haemolytic uraemic syndrome.

sections.title: Symptomatic treatment
items: Loperamide 4 mg orally, then 2 mg after each loose stool (maximum 16 mg in 24 hours), for watery diarrhoea in immunocompetent adults only. Do not use with fever, bloody stools or suspected C. difficile.
Ondansetron 4 mg orally or IV, repeated every 8 hours if needed, can help oral rehydration in vomiting patients.
Zinc is for children, not adults. Probiotics are not routinely needed.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Input and output chart, urine output, pulse and blood pressure; reassess hydration every 1 to 2 hours during IV rehydration.
Repeat electrolytes and creatinine in moderate to severe illness; watch for AKI and hypokalaemia.
Diarrhoea beyond 14 days: look for Giardia, Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora, HIV, coeliac disease and inflammatory bowel disease.

sections.title: Admit or discharge
items: Admit for severe dehydration, inability to keep up with losses orally, AKI, sepsis, severe dysentery, frailty, pregnancy with dehydration, or immunocompromise.
Discharge with ORS, hand hygiene and safe water and food advice, and return advice for blood in stool, persistent fever, reduced urine output or confusion.
Notify cholera and clusters of acute diarrhoeal disease to the district surveillance unit (IDSP).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Routine antibiotics, or fixed-dose antibiotic-antiprotozoal combinations such as ofloxacin-ornidazole, for watery diarrhoea.
Loperamide in dysentery or C. difficile infection (risk of toxic megacolon).
Empirical ciprofloxacin for dysentery or Campylobacter despite high resistance in South Asia.
Under-resuscitating cholera and missing hypokalaemia and acidosis.

drugs.name: Oral rehydration solution (reduced osmolarity)
drugs.dose: About 75 mL/kg orally over 4 hours for some dehydration, then replace ongoing losses

drugs.name: Ringer lactate
drugs.dose: 100 mL/kg IV: 30 mL/kg in 30 minutes, then 70 mL/kg over 2.5 hours
drugs.notes: Severe dehydration or shock; slower in elderly and cardiac or renal failure.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally once daily for 3 days, or 1 g orally single dose
drugs.notes: Cholera, dysentery, Campylobacter, travellers' diarrhoea. QT prolongation.

drugs.name: Ciprofloxacin
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally twice daily for 3 days
drugs.notes: Shigella (ICMR) only if susceptible or local resistance is low.

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.notes: Shigella when oral therapy is not possible. ICMR 2022 lists a single dose; continue daily, guided by culture, if bacteraemic or severely ill.

drugs.name: Metronidazole
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally three times daily for 5 days (amoebiasis); 250 mg three times daily for 5 days (giardiasis)
drugs.notes: Follow amoebiasis treatment with a luminal agent. Avoid alcohol.

drugs.name: Loperamide
drugs.dose: 4 mg orally, then 2 mg after each loose stool, maximum 16 mg per 24 hours
drugs.notes: Watery diarrhoea only; not with fever or bloody stools.
